title: Traffic Spike: Possible DDoS or Legitimate Surge
summary: The admissions website begins returning intermittent errors during a sudden traffic increase, and the on-call team must decide whether this is an attack or a legitimate surge.
learning_goals: Evaluate whether traffic evidence supports an attack hypothesis or a benign explanation
Make service-prioritization decisions under time pressure with incomplete certainty
Practice stating that evidence is inconclusive rather than defaulting to a confident conclusion
initial_situation: At 13:59, monitoring alerts fire for elevated error rates on www.campus.edu during a sharp increase in inbound traffic.

injects.message: On-call engineer asks whether this should be treated as a DDoS attack and mitigated with aggressive rate limiting.
Marketing mentions an admissions-deadline email campaign was scheduled for the same time window.
Leadership asks for a same-hour decision: block traffic aggressively, or scale up capacity and monitor.

default_objective: Assess whether the traffic pattern is more consistent with a DDoS attack or a legitimate marketing-driven surge, and recommend a response that matches the actual level of certainty in the evidence.
